agent_notes: The change is a one-line revert of a display clamp in ViewFileService.createViewFile. percentDownloaded is read by ViewFile (view-file.ts) and transfer-row.component.html (label at line 28, success class at line 33, width at line 35, ETA 'Done' branch at line 53). dashboard-stats.service.ts uses localSize, not percentDownloaded, so it is not affected.
Only the progress-bar width keeps a template-level clamp (line 35). The label, the success class and the 'Done' text all depend on the service-level clamp that was removed.
Who is affected: every user with archives that were extracted locally. The defect shows up as soon as extraction makes local_size larger than remote_size.
No API, schema or migration changes. The performance impact is negligible.
Tests: view-file.service.spec.ts:245-247 explicitly asserts the clamp ('clamps at 100, not 199%'), so this diff fails the unit suite.
Verdict: blocking. This is a regression that brings back a known display bug and fails the existing tests. Restore the clamp unless the regression is intentional.

findings.fix_hint: Restore Math.min(100, Math.trunc(100.0 * localSize / remoteSize)) along with its explanatory comment.
findings.problem: The diff removes `Math.min(100, ...)` and the comment that explained it. After extraction, local_size (unpacked) is larger than remote_size (the archive), so percentDownloaded becomes >100 (local 20 / remote 10 gives 200). I read the consumers in transfer-row.component.html. (1) Line 28 shows the raw value, so the user sees '200%' or '199%'. (2) Line 33 `[class.progress-fill--success]="file.percentDownloaded === 100"` is now false for extracted files, so the bar loses its success styling. (3) Line 53 `@else if (file.percentDownloaded === 100)` no longer matches, so the ETA column shows '-' instead of 'Done'. Only the bar width (line 35) has its own clamp. The spec at view-file.service.spec.ts:245-247 checks the clamp with vectors [20,10,100] and [100,50,100]. Those will now fail because they compute 200, so this change also fails the test suite. This puts back the bug that the old comment described.

findings.fix_hint: Restore `Math.min(100, Math.trunc(100.0 * localSize / remoteSize))` and the removed explanatory comment.
findings.problem: The diff deletes both the `Math.min(100, ...)` clamp and its explanatory comment, reverting `percentDownloaded` to the unclamped ratio `100 * localSize / remoteSize`. The removed comment explicitly documented why the clamp exists: extracted files have a local (unpacked) size larger than the remote (compressed) archive size, which produces values like 199%. This is not a speculative risk — an existing unit test (view-file.service.spec.ts lines 237-248) has test vectors `[20, 10, 100]` and `[100, 50, 100]` asserting the clamped value of 100, with an inline comment 'Extracted files: local (unpacked) > remote (archive) clamps at 100, not 199%'; this change makes that test fail.
findings.title: Removed clamp reintroduces documented >100% progress bug
findings.why_it_matters: Besides breaking the existing test suite, this value feeds UI in transfer-row.component.html: the percent text (`{{ file.percentDownloaded | number:'1.0-1' }}%`) is rendered unclamped and will display values like '199%' to users, and the exact `=== 100` checks driving the success-state class and the completed-state template branch will never match for extracted files whose local size exceeds remote size, so those transfers never visually register as complete.
